challenges.finding: Publisher reports, in Nord-Kivu, community resistance to swabbing and burials without securing (no count promoted), no free food distribution to households that day, no household given a kit (0 of 6), a low facility score card average (35.9%), and community concerns about unpaid community workers, insecurity, a missing control point, the cost of disinfectants and vaccine unavailability; in Ituri team shortages (Mangala, Mandima), IPC input stockouts (Mandima, Mambasa), a health worker strike in Tchomia, 20 patients without meals in Mandima and 7 of 43 ambulances out of service; in Haut-Uele a community refusal of a safe burial, community resistance to decontamination in Watsa and too few IPC staff in Rungu and Boma Mangbetu; in Nord-Ubangi 40 patients for 25 declared beds (160%); and in Bas-Uele only 130 of 632 providers trained in IPC-WASH, 16 of 20 priority facilities without a triage area and 17 of 20 without water supply. The Nord-Kivu vaccine stock, the Nord-Ubangi communication and supply line and the security forces line repeat SR184 without change and are not counted here. No intervention effect is established.

Contact follow-up covers five reporting provinces. Sud-Ubangi prints ND and the Bas-Uele zero is withheld after the contact cohort moved between province labels in earlier editions. The lowest printed rate is Nord-Kivu (76.7%). No zero follow-up is inferred for any province.
